subject: pharmacology
title: Oral antidiabetics and incretin therapies

steps.tx: **Metformin** starts treatment for type 2 diabetes whenever no contraindication prevents its use. It reduces hepatic glucose output, improves insulin sensitivity, stays weight neutral and never causes **hypoglycaemia** when used alone. Slow titration and extended release forms limit gastrointestinal upset in sensitive patients during initiation. Long term treatment can lower vitamin B12 levels, so clinicians screen periodically during follow up. Hypoxia, sepsis and severe renal failure raise the risk of lactic acidosis considerably.
steps.say: Metformin starts treatment for type 2 diabetes whenever no contraindication prevents its use in patients. It reduces hepatic glucose output and it never causes hypoglycaemia when clinicians use it alone. Slow titration limits gastrointestinal upset and extended release forms help sensitive patients during initiation treatment. Long term treatment lowers vitamin B12 so clinicians screen levels periodically during follow up visits.

steps.tx: **Sulfonylureas** such as glipizide and glimepiride force pancreatic insulin release regardless of the blood glucose level. That glucose independent action explains **hypoglycaemia** and weight gain during treatment in many patients. Older patients and those with renal failure suffer prolonged lows, especially with long acting agents. Meglitinides act briefly at meal times and patients skip the dose when they miss a meal. Short acting agents suit elderly patients better because prolonged hypoglycaemia threatens them most.
steps.say: Sulfonylureas force pancreatic insulin release regardless of the blood glucose level in patients taking them daily. That glucose independent action explains hypoglycaemia and weight gain during treatment in many patients overall. Older patients suffer prolonged lows because renal failure slows clearance of long acting agents considerably. Meglitinides act briefly at meal times and patients skip doses when meals get missed. Short acting agents suit elderly patients better because prolonged hypoglycaemia threatens them most seriously.

steps.tx: **Pioglitazone** activates nuclear receptors and improves insulin sensitivity in resistant tissues over weeks. It retains fluid and can precipitate **heart failure**, so clinicians avoid it when cardiac function already fails. Treatment also raises fracture risk and carries a debated association with bladder cancer in studies. Sitagliptin and related drugs stay weight neutral and rarely cause hypoglycaemia when used alone. Acarbose blocks carbohydrate digestion in the gut and it produces flatulence from colonic fermentation.
steps.say: Pioglitazone improves insulin sensitivity in resistant tissues but it retains fluid in many patients treated. That fluid retention can precipitate heart failure so clinicians avoid it when cardiac function fails already. Treatment also raises fracture risk during longer courses of therapy in older patients treated. Sitagliptin stays weight neutral and it rarely causes hypoglycaemia when clinicians use it alone. Acarbose blocks carbohydrate digestion and it produces flatulence from colonic fermentation after meals daily.

steps.tx: This chest radiograph shows **cardiogenic pulmonary oedema** with a perihilar bat wing pattern of shadowing. The heart looks enlarged and short **Kerley B lines** mark fluid in the interlobular septa at the bases. Pioglitazone retains fluid through renal sodium handling and it can unmask latent heart failure in this way. A breathless diabetic patient gaining weight on treatment should trigger exactly this imaging thought. Stopping the drug and treating cardiac failure addresses the cause behind the picture.

steps.tx: **GLP 1 receptor agonists** such as semaglutide and liraglutide reduce weight and cause nausea during dose escalation. Clinicians avoid this class with a history of **medullary thyroid cancer** or related endocrine syndromes in the family. Drugs that increase urinary glucose excretion improve heart failure and kidney outcomes in type 2 diabetes. Euglycaemic ketoacidosis remains the feared trap with that kidney protective class during acute illness. Comorbidity now drives add on choice after metformin, with cardiac and renal benefit leading decisions.
steps.say: Drugs in the incretin class reduce weight and they cause nausea during dose escalation in patients. Clinicians avoid this class when medullary thyroid cancer or related syndromes affect the family history. Drugs that increase urinary glucose excretion improve heart failure and kidney outcomes in diabetes considerably. Euglycaemic ketoacidosis remains the feared trap during acute illness with that kidney protective class used. Comorbidity now drives add on choice because cardiac and renal benefit leads prescribing decisions today.
